newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN SAYS JOINT EMU FISCAL POLICY OK - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN SAYS JOINT EMU FISCAL POLICY OK - PAPER.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was quoted as saying that he saw no ideological problems with a common fiscal policy in European economic and monetary union in due course.
"Personally, I don't find it difficult from an ideological point of view that fiscal policy is integrated in due course," Lipponen said in an interview in Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet on Monday.
Lipponen said preparations for the single currency had come so far that there was now "enormous pressure" for EMU to succeed despite economic problems in Germany and France.
He reiterated that Finland was preparing to join the third stage of EMU from day one.
"It would look rather odd if we will meet the criteria and then not want to participate," Lipponen said.

"For us, it is a reality that our industry and business will work under all circumstances with the new euro currency. For us, it is a reality that the countries in EMU will become a new, inner circle which one one must also be part of if one wants to influence future policy," he said.
"These realities are more important for us than they seem to be for Swedish politicians," he added.
